newsitem.title: USA: IMF releases further $350 million to Russia.
newsitem.headline: IMF releases further $350 million to Russia.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund's board released a further tranche of roughly $350 million to Russia under a previously-approved $10.2 billion loan programme, IMF officials said on Wednesday.
"The board meeting went fine," one official, who declined to be named, said. "The next tranche is ready for disbursement."
The approval of the latest tranche of the loan had been expected. IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus said last week that the multilateral agency's programme with Russia was going well.

"In spite of the enormous difficulty that Russia has been living with for some time, Russia is complying with the programme," Camdessus said at the end of the annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank.
The IMF reviews Russia's economy monthly to ensure the country is meeting previously agreed on economic targets. The IMF released $350 million to Russia in September.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Tuesday promised to bring inflation down next year and said the government would not give in to the temptation to loosen monetary policy and print extra rubles.
Chernomyrdin said Russia's key budget task was to raise revenues as there was no way to cut spending further.
The lower house of the Russian parliament is due to debate the 1997 budget on Friday.
The IMF in the past has urged Russia to close tax loopholes and take other measures to boost government revenue.
The Russian government recently froze the assets of gas giant Gazprom in a bid to recover $2.8 billion in back taxes.
A finance ministry official said in Moscow last week that the move should set an example to other major companies to pay their taxes on time.
